trust_decision.summary: Before running git, the library decides whether caller kwargs spell a blocked option (e.g. -u/--upload-pack, -c, -o, -F). The candidate list is built in Git._option_candidates and judged in Git.check_unsafe_options. With split_single_char_options=False, the candidate list held only '-<key>' while argv got '-<key><value>', so a short option smuggled into the value was never checked.

landing_point.why: The advisory names split_single_char_options and short-option token smuggling. Grepping that flag leads straight to _option_candidates (git/cmd.py:1042) and transform_kwarg (git/cmd.py:1628-1631).

fix_sites.entry_point: Every guarded public API that builds candidates with Git._option_candidates(..., kwargs): Repo.clone/clone_from (git/repo/base.py:1479-1482), Repo.archive (git/repo/base.py:1701-1704), TagReference.create (git/refs/tag.py:138-141), Repo.iter_commits/blame/blame_incremental, Commit.count/iter_items, Diffable.diff, IndexFile.diff/checkout, Remote.fetch/pull/push, Git.ls_remote
fix_sites.module_kind: shared core helper (command-line option candidate builder)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fix makes candidates match argv exactly ('-aFfile', '-9o/path'). Whether those clusters are blocked depends on check_unsafe_options' hard-coded clusterable set (git/cmd.py:1008), which is written for clone/fetch flags. A solver can argue that tag/archive flag clustering is a separate checker limitation, not split_single_char_options smuggling.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Joined safe short values must keep working: diff with split_single_char_options=False, M='75%' gives -M75% (test/test_diff.py:510,524), and -oupstream/-bcurrent must not be rejected (test/test_git.py:200-203, docstring git/cmd.py:985-987). If a fix rejects any unsplit short option, or treats every joined character as an option, these break.

O6_input_shapes: single-char kwarg with scalar str value and split_single_char_options=False (-nuhelper)
single-char kwarg with list/tuple of values (one joined token per value)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: TagReference.create with a non-clusterable value-less tag flag joined to blocked -F (kwarg a='F<path>', split_single_char_options=False gives -aF<path>). The clusterable set lacks 'a', so the scan stops before 'F'.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The clusterable set is documented as Git's value-less flags (git/cmd.py:1005-1007). Tag's -a/-e are a neighbouring command's flags, not a split_single_char_options issue.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: check is in git/cmd.py; the route enters from git/refs/tag.py:137-158 (different package, git/refs)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Repo.archive with a compression-level digit flag joined to blocked -o (kwarg '9'='o<path>', split_single_char_options=False gives -9o<path>). Digits other than 4/6 are not in the clusterable set.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Digit kwargs are an odd, unsupported-looking shape (**{'9': ...}). The set already has 4/6 for fetch/clone, so a solver can argue digits were considered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: check in git/cmd.py; route enters from git/repo/base.py:1700-1711 (git/repo package)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: TagReference.create passes positional path/reference to git tag without '--', and candidates are built from kwargs only, so a tag name starting with '-F' reaches git as an option.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Positional arguments are tag names, not options. The guard is documented as kwarg-based, and this is not the split-option mechanism.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add a short alias to fetch/pull/push unsafe lists (or a guarded Remote API whose unsafe list has a short option) so split_single_char_options=False smuggling also reaches git/remote.py
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Other lists already pair long and short spellings (git/repo/base.py:145-151, git/refs/tag.py:46), so a maintainer extending these would follow the same pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: set_persistent_git_options/Git.__call__ build options with transform_kwargs and no unsafe-option check; a guarded variant that forwards split_single_char_options would be a second candidate builder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A wrapper reaching the same transform_kwargs mapper is the existing code shape (git/cmd.py:1111, 1673).

O9_family: argument injection (CWE-88): option guard bypass via a candidate list that diverges from the real argv

O10_build.toolchain: pip / pytest; needs a git binary on PATH
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_git.py:159-233 (check_unsafe_options/_option_candidates unit tests), test/test_diff.py:510-524 (unsplit -M), plus test_clone/test_remote unsafe-option tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Append f'-{key}{value}' to candidates when split is False (exactly the published fix), then stop, trusting check_unsafe_options' clusterable set to judge every joined token.

out_of_scope_notes: git/refs/tag.py:164 TagReference.delete passes tag names to 'git tag -d' without '--'; not the unsafe-option guard path.
11 sibling advisories on the same guard family suggest the guard has been patched repeatedly; recall may be higher than this single CVE suggests.
unverified: That git's parse-options treats 'git tag -aF<path>' and 'git archive -9o<path>' as clustered -a/-9 plus -F/-o; reasoned from git's option definitions, not executed.
present_in_latest for every O8 route: no latest release supplied.
repo_mb: repository size not measured, so tiny_repo is neither confirmed nor ruled out (GitPython is a small library; the lessons say small libraries rarely produced hard tasks).

O1 counts guarded entry points whose unsafe list contains a short option (clone, clone_from, archive, iter_commits, blame, blame_incremental, Commit.count, Commit.iter_items, Diffable.diff, IndexFile.diff, TagReference.create); Submodule add/update reach clone indirectly and are not counted separately.
O13 recall_risk is a judgement from 11 sibling advisories; not checked against write-ups.
